command: uv run python scripts/measure_slm_slots.py --grounding-accuracy --arm cloud --limit 20 --corpus-dir corpus --out .benchmark-reports/ga-cloud-off.json
benchmark_input: the same assembled corpus the local arm uses, built locally from the repository's tracked fixtures: 96 clause units from 17 tracked fixture documents (tests/fixtures/**/*.txt verbatim plus fixture PDFs/DOCX parsed with openreview_cli.parsing), scoring the first 20 units; PII stripped before every model call, so the clause text and positive claims are the stripped text sent for cloud egress. Not the CUAD corpus the earlier cloud receipt used
notes: Run on this machine with the configured cloud slots, model openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, second question OFF (the shipped default). This was a local (non-CI) run, so the harness recorded git_sha "unknown" (it reads only GITHUB_SHA); the commit recorded here is the branch tip the run was made at, from branch feat/grounding-recall as pushed. The benchmark input is the same assembled corpus the local arm uses — the repository's tracked fixtures assembled locally into a corpus directory (96 clause units from 17 documents), scoring the first 20 — and PII was stripped before every model call (51 entities replaced) with the review path's own strip_pii_clauses machinery, so the clause text and positive claims are the stripped text sent for cloud egress. This is a different corpus from the older CUAD-based grounding-accuracy-cloud receipt it replaces, so the two are not comparable. Positives and negatives come in classes that include paraphrases: 25 positives (20 clause qualifying sentences plus 5 lightly rewritten copies) and 44 negatives (20 unsupported_claim + 20 hallucination + 4 paraphrased_unsupported); paraphrases_skipped counts a rewrite that equalled its source (31 this run). Both positive classes are supported by the clause by construction and the substitution map is narrow, so no real-world false-positive rate may be quoted; the negative arm is the signal. Single-sample smoke measurement, not a benchmark: model replies vary run to run. Costs money per run (69 calls this run).
